question: If ordinary feedback favors averaging independent seeds, do group-held training panels support overriding that choice on never-seen profiles? This is a secondary exploratory decision study using already admitted control fits.
design: Reuse the default and seed-averaged components for the exact two full-resource population comparison panels. For rows with a fitting-unknown profile, allow restoration of the pre-pilot probabilities. On known profiles always retain ordinary predictions. Permit the override only if the ordinary policy actually adopted repeats, the move is nonnegative in accuracy on each inner panel, pooled net gain is at least 0.20 percentage points, and pooled Brier does not worsen. Score the resulting decisions on the two stress folds after all study decisions are saved. No new model fits or outcome-based threshold selection.
boundary: This reuses the group-held folds and cannot establish a course result. Only if more than one fold is eligible, at least one improves, neither loses and pooled gains exceed 0.30 percentage points is a prospective replication warranted.
